item.title: Ripley's bought my Etch A Sketch art!
item.description: I am thrilled to share that I've been working with Ripley's over the years which has led to many incredible adventures. So it means the world to me that they purchased my most ambitious Etch A Sketch series to date! If you visit the Grand Prairie location you can vote for my art through the end of the month which can in theory provide some extra capital for what I'm sure will be a Very Silly Pursuit :) Can't make it to Grand Prairie? Come see me in Orlando on Labor Day! I'll be making free art portraits with Ripley's from 2-4 at Icon Park. Can't make it to Orlando either? Ah well, hopefully you'll find a little placard about me and my art at a future Ripley's visit! Thank you all for the amazing support - the only reason Ripley's reached out to me was because I hit the front page of Reddit a few years ago. Sometimes upvotes really do matter, and I think that's pretty peachy keen.

item.title: Intense acting by Sidney Poitier in "Guess who's coming to dinner?" (1967) #REAL TALK
item.description: NOT SO FUN FACT: Spencer Tracy, who plays the white father was dying while the film was being shot. Co- star, Katherine Hepburn, and director, Stanley Kramer, both put up their salaries as backing because the studio didn't want to insure an actor who could possibly die in the middle of production. The very last scene in the film is the very last scene that Tracy appeared in; he died 17 days after it was filmed.

item.title: GovBrief Today #561
item.description: At least three sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln have reportedly tried to jump into the ocean, but Trump says their deployment is "not nearly long enough." He has kept the carrier at sea for nine months fighting his Iran war, including a record 208 straight days without touching land. This week, crew member families broke their silence, describing meals of half a cup of rice and two tortillas, and weeks without hot water. When a reporter told Trump on Friday that they were worried, he said, "No, they're not." The Navy insists suicide attempts aboard have not risen. But on August 3, a rescue helicopter pulled a sailor from the sea. Trump promised the Lincoln will be swapped for "another very similar ship." His plan is one boat replacing another, with 5,000 people aboard whose families he refuses to hear. I've emailed 8,655 stories over 561 straight nights, free and without ads. The algorithm can't show them all to you. Add your email address at govbrief.today and I will. I.C.E. is just part of A.C.A.B. https://policebrutalitycenter.org/police-brutality/statistics/ Edit: In 2022, Assistant Chief Adam Glueck, of the Cape Girardeau Police Department in southeastern Missouri, purchased electric shock gloves for his officers after learning about them at a trade show. And his employees, he said, couldn’t get enough of them. “If I try to take away the gloves from those officers at this point I think we may have a mutiny on our hands,” Glueck joked on a podcast interview a couple of years later. “They’ve grown really attached.” The shock gloves, he went on to explain, allow their wearer to inflict pain without leaving the sort of marks that could look bad to witnesses or leave an officer vulnerable to lawsuits. “In today’s society, you know, everybody’s filming everything, everybody has a cell phone,” Glueck said. If an officer punches someone on camera, that can go viral in an instant; even a standard taser leaves puncture wounds. But “the glove is low optic, and it looks better on camera, and it looks better to those witnesses. With a glove, there are no burn marks or scars.” https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2026/08/ice-shock-gloves-torture-compliant-technologies-jeff-niklaus/ The place selling the gloves to cops are https://www.complianttechnologies.net/the-glove
